what: One oscillator that morphs from a saw, through a triangle, to a pulse wave as you turn SHAPE.
how: A variable-shape oscillator makes one wave whose outline changes smoothly with SHAPE. PW (pulse width) changes the proportions of the pulse wave. With SYNC on, the wave restarts at a second, faster frequency (the pitch times RATIO), which gives a tearing, bright sound that changes as RATIO is swept.

ins.pitch: Pitch in octaves (1 volt per octave, 0 is middle C). Patch KEYS' pitch here.
ins.shape: A control signal that adds to SHAPE (each 1.0 adds 0.5). Patch an LFO or ENV to morph the wave.
ins.pwm: A control signal that adds to PW (each 1.0 adds 0.4). An LFO here is the classic pulse-width modulation, a moving, chorus-like tone.

knobs.shape: The wave shape, 0 to 1: a saw at one end, a triangle in the middle, a pulse at the top.
knobs.pw: The pulse width, 0 to 1. 0.5 is a symmetrical square when SHAPE is at the pulse end; it only matters there.
knobs.tune: Shifts the pitch in semitones, -24 to 24 (two octaves down to two up), added to the pitch input.
knobs.sync: OFF or ON. ON restarts the wave at the pitch times RATIO, for a hard-sync sound.
knobs.ratio: The sync frequency compared to the pitch, 0.5 to 8. Only matters when SYNC is ON; sweeping it makes the classic sync whoosh.

try: Patch KEYS' pitch into SHAPER's pitch, SHAPER's out through a VCA into OUT, and an LFO into the pwm input. Hold a note and sweep SHAPE from saw to pulse; then turn SYNC on and move RATIO.
